question: An intrinsic semiconductor crystal has a defined forbidden energy gap ($E_g$) of $1.5 \text{ eV}$. An electron residing exactly at the highest available energy level of the Valence Band ($E_V$) is subjected to an incident photon possessing an energy of $1.2 \times 10^{-19} \text{ Joules}$. Applying the principles of Energy Band Theory, what will be the physical outcome for this specific electron? (Assume $1 \text{ eV} = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ J}$).

options.A: The electron will transition to the conduction band and possess a residual kinetic energy of $0.75 \text{ eV}$.
options.B: The electron will transition into the middle of the forbidden energy gap and remain temporarily trapped there.
options.C: The electron cannot absorb the photon and will remain in its current state within the valence band.
options.D: The electron will absorb the photon, move to the conduction band, and immediately fall back, emitting a $1.5 \text{ eV}$ photon.
